thread.title: Apple to push fix for locating 911 callers - MarketWatch

author: Sarah Krouse
title: Apple to push fix for locating 911 callers - MarketWatch
text:
Published: June 18, 2018 8:11 a.m. ET Share
Apple’s move is a sign that smartphone makers are willing to step into America’s emergency response infrastructure, an area ripe for upgrades Getty Images
By Sarah Krouse
Apple Inc. is partnering with a startup to tackle a problem that has long vexed 911 operators: locating cellphone callers.
Most 911 calls are made using mobile phones, but those callers’ locations are harder to pinpoint than those of calls made using traditional land lines — a problem that can delay first responders.
RapidSOS, an upstart backed by three former Federal Communications Commission leaders, aimed to solve that problem. It created technology that pipes location information from smartphones and other internet-connected devices directly into the software used within 911 call centers.
Apple’s AAPL, -1.03% new partnership with RapidSOS means iPhone users who call 911 will automatically send their location to emergency call centers, representatives for the companies said. Apple plans to push the new software to iPhones later this year as part of an update to its iOS mobile software, the company said.
